content.text:
I found the official Claude Code overview page, and the main thing to know is that it has moved to a new web address.

**Where the official docs are now**

Anthropic's GitHub repo for Claude Code points to its
official documentation
at
code.claude.com/docs/en/overview
. A third-party directory also says
the official Claude Code documentation lives at code.claude.com/docs/en/.
The old address,
https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/overview

, still shows up in search results with the same overview page.

**What the overview page says**

- **What it is:**
A coding tool that can read your codebase, edit files, run commands and connect to your development tools. You can use it in the terminal, an IDE, a desktop app or the browser.
- **What you need to use it:**
Most versions need a Claude subscription or an Anthropic Console account. The terminal version, VS Code and JetBrains also work with third-party providers.
- **Terminal:**

On Linux you can also install with apt, dnf or apk (Debian, Fedora, RHEL and Alpine). Then go to your project folder and run `claude`. It asks you to log in the first time, unless you've set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable and approve using that key.
- **VS Code:**
Search for "Claude Code" in the Extensions view. After installing, open the Command Palette, type "Claude Code" and choose Open in New Tab.
- **Desktop app:**
A separate app where you can review changes visually, run several sessions side by side, schedule recurring tasks and start cloud sessions. It's available for macOS and Windows.
- **Next step:** The page links to a
Quickstart that walks you through a first real task, from exploring a codebase to committing a fix.

**Other official Anthropic resources**

- **Product page (claude.com/product/claude-code):**
Suggests giving Claude a bug fix, a test or a migration that takes several days, and then checking its work from your terminal, IDE, Slack or the web.
It runs on macOS, Linux and Windows.
- **GitHub repo (github.com/anthropics/claude-code):**
You can use it in your terminal or IDE, or tag @claude on GitHub.
- **Claude Platform docs (platform.claude.com/docs):** This is the main documentation site for Anthropic's API. It also links to Claude Code, calling it
an agentic coding assistant in your terminal.
- **"How Anthropic teams use Claude Code" (PDF):** Examples from Anthropic's own teams. For instance,
the security engineering team wrote half of all the custom slash commands in Anthropic's main shared codebase.

**One conflicting source**

The freeCodeCamp Claude Code Handbook tells readers to
go to code.claude.ai and calls it Anthropic's official installation hub for Claude Code.

That doesn't match the code.claude.com address on Anthropic's own GitHub repo, so I'd trust code.claude.com.

**Unofficial guides**

If you also want guides written by users,
ClaudeLog covers practical tips, ways to get more out of the tool and community best practices
. Tons of Skills keeps
an organized list of the official docs on skills, plugins, agents, hooks, MCP, the command line and best practices
